item.title: Arsenic and Old Lace [Live Theatre] — Sun Oct 11, 2:30 PM — Brown County Playhouse
item.description:
Drama critic Mortimer Brewster’s engagement announcement is upended when he discovers a corpse in his elderly aunts’ window seat. Mortimer rushes to tell Abby and Martha before they stumble upon the body themselves, only to learn that the two old women aren’t just aware of the dead man in their parlor, they killed him! Between his aunts’ penchant for poisoning wine, a brother who thinks he’s Teddy Roosevelt, and another brother using plastic surgery to hide from the police – not to mention Mortimer’s own hesitancy about marriage – it’ll be a miracle if Mortimer makes it to his wedding. Arsenic and Old Lace is a classic dark comedy about the only thing more deadly than poison: family.
Abby Brewster: Becky Stapf Martha Brewster: Amy Frazer Rev. Dr. Harper: Mike Harold Teddy Brewster: Jerry Maguire Officer Brophy: Mark Webber Officer Klein: Devon Davis Elaine Harper: Shaun Ancelet Mortimer Brewster: Ben Sledge Mr. Gibbs: Jackson Flora Jonathan Brewster: Horace Tucker Dr. Einstein: Steve

item.title: Memory Transformed Concert: The Sway Machinery & The Immortal Khazntes — Sun Oct 11, 7:00 PM — Auer Hall - IU Bloomington
item.description:
The Borns Jewish Studies Program presents the culminating concert of Memory Transformed: Materials of Heritage in Jewish Eastern European Life, featuring The Sway Machinery and The Immortal Khazntes. Bringing together musicians whose work engages deeply with Jewish musical traditions, the concert explores the continuing life and transformation of Eastern European Jewish music through contemporary performance. The concert concludes a full day of Memory Transformed programming at Indiana University Bloomington, including a symposium on Jewish cultural heritage and material culture, an afternoon reception at the Eskenazi Museum of Art, and guided museum tours.Free and open to the public. Registration is encouraged but not required; no ticket is required for entry. Please visit the Memory Transformed event webpage for the latest program and location information.
Source: Eskenazi Museum of Art, IU Jacobs School of Music

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Mon Oct 12 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Oct 12 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Mon Oct 12 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Wed Oct 14 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Wed Oct 14 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Wed Oct 14 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. item.title: Guest Music Theory Lecture – Jonathan De Souza (Western University, Ontario), "Music Theory and Practice: A Violin-Based Analysis of 'Salut d'amour'" — Thu Oct 15, 5:00 PM — Ford-Crawford Hall
item.description: Abstract Music theory has traditionally focused on abstract musical structures and idealized listeners. Yet in recent years, the discipline has increasingly considered performance, embodiment, instruments, and related issues. So, current theory engages practice. How can we think about this apparent paradigm shift? And more generally, about the relation between music theory and practice? In this talk, I'll approach these questions while developing an analysis of Edward Elgar's Salut d'amour, op. 12, that draws on my experience as a theorist and a lifelong violinist. Ultimately, I'll argue that theory and practice, like mind and body, are fundamentally interconnected.Five Friends Master Class Series – Honoring Robert SamelsThe Five Friends Master Class Series honoring the lives of five talented Jacobs School of Music students—Chris Carducci, Garth Eppley, Georgina Joshi, Zachary Novak, and Robert Samelswas established in 2012 with a gift of $1 million from the Georgina Joshi Foundation,
